title: Data Watermarking for Sequential Recommender Systems

problem.claim: Data watermarking for sequential recommender systems embeds a watermark into a target dataset so it can be detected in models trained on that dataset.

contributions.claim: The authors present Dataset Watermarking for Recommender Systems (DWRS) for dataset and user watermarking.
DWRS represents the watermark by placing consecutive items within interaction sequences from normal users.
DWRS defines a Receptive Field to guide watermark insertion and facilitate watermark memorization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments across five representative sequential recommendation models and three benchmark datasets.
The authors report that DWRS effectively protects data copyright while preserving model utility.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large-scale, high-quality data is important for high-performance AI systems, increasing attention to data copyright protection.
The work investigates data watermarking for sequential recommender systems, including dataset-level and user-level protection.
DWRS inserts consecutive-item watermarks into interaction sequences and uses a Receptive Field to guide insertion.
Experiments cover five sequential recommendation models and three benchmark datasets, with reported copyright protection and preserved model utility.

source_observation.claim: The watermark is embedded in user interaction sequences and designed to be memorized by trained models.

interpretation.claim: A data watermark can use model-training behavior as the mechanism for later ownership detection.

application.claim: For sequential recommendation data, consider embedding structured item sequences while accounting for how insertion affects model memorization.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond sequential recommender systems or other data modalities.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the watermark detection procedure or detection criteria.
The abstract does not describe the Receptive Field construction or insertion algorithm.
The abstract does not provide experimental metrics, baselines, or numerical results.
The abstract does not quantify the trade-off between copyright protection and model utility.
